result.title: Do Self-Evolving Skills Generalize to Held-Out Tasks?
result.summary: AI agents can externalize what they learn from past tasks into reusable \emph{skills}, such as procedures, checklists, code, or other executable artifacts, that can be retrieved and reused when solving new tasks. Self-evolving skill methods keep rewriting these skills after each round of practice on training tasks, and the skill is then used on new tasks of the same kind. We ask a question: does the improvement a skill shows on its training tasks carry over to new test tasks? We test five self-evolving methods and a one-shot skill on six benchmarks, with the same model, the same agent, and the same train/test split for every method. Of the 21 skills that improve on their training tasks, 5 keep all of that improvement on the test tasks, 13 keep part of it, and 3 keep none of it. No existing method is best everywhere. When we read the skills, the ones that carry over badly often fix details that should depend on the task, such as column names and output files, or turn a fix for one failure into a rule for every task. An LLM judge that reads the skill content can often see this: it ranks finished skills the same way the test results do in 86\% of pairs. But it predicts the effect of a single edit poorly, so edits still have to be tested by running them. Based on these findings, we describe Generalizable Skill Optimization (GSO), which keeps only a guide for writing skills and writes a new skill for each task; it scores highest on all six benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文系统检验五种自演化 skill 方法在训练任务上的提升能否泛化到同类的留出测试任务，六个基准上 21 个 skill 中仅 5 个完全迁移、13 个部分迁移、3 个完全不迁移，并据此提出只保留写作指南、每个任务重新生成 skill 的 GSO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「训练收益是否迁移到留出任务」的问题设定与轨迹训练、贡献分配及泛化评价可类比，skill 内容审查与 LLM judge 预测单次编辑失效的发现，可能为 latent 状态监督与停止决策提供核查线索。
